name: A1
description: CEFR A1 入门级核心词，适合英语零基础起步。

words.definition: the number 6
examples: Look for a bus with a number six on the front of it.; "How many grandchildren do you have now?" "I've got six (grandchildren)."; My place [has] six rooms.

words.definition: to be born, got from, or made in a particular place
examples: She comes from Italy.; Where do you come from?; Some of the best wines come from France.; Does that quote come from Shakespeare?; She could hear banging coming from the room upstairs.

words.definition: If you have American/British/Swiss, etc. nationality, you are legally a member of that country.
examples: She has British nationality.; He has dual nationality.; What nationality are you?; At the International School they have pupils of 46 different nationalities.; My friend [was] born in Norway, but his nationality is Polish.

words.definition: used to refer to a time between twelve o'clock at night and twelve o'clock in the middle of the day
examples: We're open between 9 a.m.
and 5 p.m.
daily.; The first election results are expected around 1 a.m.; I go to college [from] 9.15 a.m.

words.definition: the number 13
examples: eleven, twelve, thirteen, fourteen; Some people think that thirteen is an unlucky number.; Dear Joshua, I'm writing to tell you that I am now thirteen Years old.

words.definition: used to agree with a suggestion, idea, etc.
examples: "Shall we meet at 8 o'clock?" "Yes, that's fine."; OK that's fine.
We['ll] meet at 8pm.

words.definition: remember
examples: Don't forget your homework!; Don't forget to lock the door.; Don't forget that classes start at 2.0 this afternoon.; And please don't forget the des[s]ert!

words.definition: to reach or arrive at a particular place
examples: We got home later than usual.; I didn't get to work till nine o'clock.; I had a good time at your house last night but when I got home I realized I had forg[o]tten my bag!

words.definition: a mobile phone
examples: Can I use your mobile?; It's a very modern mobile, it's [a] Nokia and it's made in Finland.

words.definition: something you say when you leave someone or they leave you in the evening, or when you are going to bed
examples: Good night, everyone - I'm off to bed.

words.definition: the number 19
examples: eighteen, nineteen, twenty; Her daughter is nineteen.; I [had a] birthday [party] in my house when I [became] nineteen.

words.definition: used to refer to a time after midday but before midnight
examples: We'll be arriving at about 4.30 p.m.; The 6 p.m.
train is usually very crowded.; See you tomorrow at 7 p.m.

words.definition: the system that connects computers all over the world and allows people who use computers to look at websites
examples: I found out about the book on the Internet.; a company that provides cheap Internet access; She uses the Internet every day.

words.definition: the number 11
examples: nine, ten, eleven, twelve; There are eleven girls in my class and fifteen boys.; I invited ten or eleven friends.

words.definition: the number 16
examples: fourteen, fifteen, sixteen, seventeen; We've got sixteen (people) coming for lunch.; Hi!
My name is Ian and I'm sixteen years old.

words.definition: used for saying goodbye to someone you are going to meet again soon
examples: I'll see you soon!; See you soon.

words.definition: to photograph someone or something
examples: Did you take any pictures of the sunset?; She took some great photos of the children.; He had his photograph taken by a professional.; Sometimes I take photos [of] them and I feed these bird[s].

words.definition: to a large amount or degree
examples: Thank you very much for the flowers!; I like her very much.; I like Bradford very much.

words.definition: a large pink, brown or black farm animal with short legs and a curved tail, kept for its meat
examples: The meat produced from a pig is called pork, bacon or ham.; a pig farm; There is a small pink pig on it.

words.definition: the number 7
examples: The restaurant opens for dinner at seven o'clock.; We're open seven days a week.; Tomorrow I'll finish my work at six o'clock, so I think that I'll can arrive your home at seven o'clock.

words.definition: more than one person
examples: Many people never take any exercise.; We've invited thirty people to our party.; I like this place because there are many shops around and many people.

words.definition: an alcoholic drink which is usually made from grapes, or sometimes from other fruit
examples: a wine cellar/glass; red/white/dry/sweet/sparkling wine; Shall we have a bottle/glass of wine with dinner?; I love Australian wines, especially the white wines.; Would you like to see the wine list, sir?

words.definition: used before adjectives and adverbs to mean 'more than is allowed, necessary, possible, etc.'
examples: Do you think this jacket is too big for me?;  There are too many cars on the roads these days.
;  We enjoyed the film but it was much too long.
; There were far too many people for such a small room.; [Maths] is too hard for me sometimes.

words.definition: a piece of equipment in the shape of a box, with a screen on the front, used for watching programmes
examples: a flat-screen television; Could you turn the television down?; I want to sell my small television.

words.definition: 30 minutes past one o'clock/two o'clock/three o'clock, etc.
examples: We got back to our hotel at half past seven.
; I start college at half past nine.

words.definition: a boy or girl who is not yet an adult, or a son or daughter of any age
examples: an eight-year-old child; As a child I didn't eat vegetables.; A small group of children waited outside the door.; Both her children are now married with children of their own.; Jan is married with three young children.

words.definition: the time between a person's birth and their death
examples: Life's too short to worry about money!; I'm not sure I want to spend the rest of my life with him.; Unfortunately, accidents are part of life.; He doesn't know what he really wants in/out of life.; He lost his life in the Great War.

words.definition: your possessions or a set of objects
examples: I'll just get my things together and we can go.; All their things were destroyed in the fire.; Bring your swimming things if the weather's nice.; I like this place because the people are happy to work for example [on] a farm and they don't need a lot of things [to] be happy.

words.definition: making you healthy or happy
examples: Swimming is really good for you.; It's good for you to eat plenty of vegetables.; I think playing basketball is good for you.

words.definition: If you need to do something, it is necessary to do it.
examples: I need to do some shopping on my way home from work.
I need to go to the toilet.
Do we need to go with her?
I need to learn English.

words.definition: to breathe smoke into your mouth from a cigarette
examples: Do you mind if I smoke?; I used to smoke a packet of cigarettes a day.; I like the pause between lesson[s].
We go outside [to] smoke and fool about.

words.definition: a telephone that you can carry everywhere with you
examples: I've left my mobile phone at home.; I'm very happy because I bought a new mobile phone.

words.definition: an adult male human being
examples: a young/tall man; men and women; the man in the green jacket; the men's 400 metres champion; He's a very good man.

words.definition: used to ask someone if they want something
examples: Would you like a drink?; Would you like to eat now?; Would you like to come?

words.definition: a short letter
examples: He left a note to say he would be home late.; Did you get my note?; There's a note pinned to the door saying when the shop will open again.; Hi Rie Thank you for your note to me!

words.definition: television
examples: What's on TV tonight?; You watch too much TV!; We ate in front of the TV.; TV personalities; She watch[e]s TV every evening.

words.definition: the activity of moving your feet and your body to the rhythm of music
examples: Shall we go dancing tonight?; He likes football, dancing, and snowboarding.

words.definition: the evening or night that has just passed
examples: I didn't sleep well last night.; Did you go out last night?; I think I left my coat in your house last night.

words.definition: used to give an example of the type of thing you mean
examples: I like soft fruit, for example, peaches and plums.; Some people, students for example, can get cheaper tickets.; Also he likes to do sports, for example swimming and c[ycl]ing.

words.definition: the number 18
examples: seventeen, eighteen, nineteen; an eighteen-storey building; I want to sell a bike.
It is eighteen years old.

words.definition: a set of questions to measure someone's knowledge or ability
examples: She had to take an aptitude test as part of the interview.; He passed/failed the written test.; I do writing, spelling test[s], speaking, etc.

words.definition: the form of the verb which is used to show what happens or exists now
examples: All the verbs in this text are in the present.

words.definition: If something is possible, it can happen or be done.
examples: Is it possible to speak to the manager please?; Please send it today, if possible.; Is it possible to buy tickets in advance?; If possible, I would like to eat lasagne, because I love Italian food.

words.definition: a machine that is used for playing music CDs
examples: She has a CD player in her bedroom.; My cousin bought me a CD player and I got a box of chocolate[s] from my friends.

words.definition: used to ask someone if they are well and happy
examples: "Hi, Lucy, how are you?" "Fine, thanks, how are you?"; Dear Ramesh, How are you?

words.definition: the number 3
examples: I've got three sisters.; School finishes at three o'clock.; I have three daughters.

words.definition: also
examples: Are you going to invite Steve as well?; Dylma goes to school every day and work[s] as well.

words.definition: used to tell someone that they do not need to think about something or do anything about something
examples: Don't worry - she'll be all right.; Don't worry about phoning Ian - I'll do it later.; Don't worry about dinner, because I eat everything.

words.definition: to have your home somewhere
examples: Where do you live?; We live in London.; Some students live on the University campus.; He lives with four other people in a shared house.; I live in Springfield.

words.definition: a human being
examples: He's a very dangerous person.; You're the only person I know at this party.; Who was the first person to swim the English Channel?; A meal at the restaurant costs about £35 per person.; She's [a] very good person.
I really like my friends.

words.definition: one of the two flat parts on the ends of your legs that you stand on
examples: I've hurt my left foot.;  bare feet; Then, in just a few minutes, we are going to put our feet in the hot sand.

words.definition: the number 12
examples: ten, eleven, twelve, thirteen; a twelve-seater minibus; We can start at twelve o'clock.

words.definition: the number 4
examples: Most animals have four legs.; We need four people to make up a team.; He works four days and has four days off.

words.definition: to be a particular age
examples: Her son is six years old.; He is 53 years old [and] he live[s] in Madeira.

words.definition: an alcoholic drink made from grain
examples: a pint of beer; Would you like another beer?; This beer is brewed in Mexico.; She likes drink[ing] beer and sometimes goes to the nightclub.

words.definition: Someone who is slim is thin in an attractive way.
examples: slim hips/legs; She's got a lovely slim figure.; She is tall and slim.

words.definition: to give money to someone because you are buying something from them, or because you owe them money
examples: Helena paid for the meal.; He paid £200 for the tickets.; Would you prefer to pay by cash or card?; Did you pay the telephone bill?; I [don't] have to pay.
It's free.

words.definition: used to accept something politely
examples: "Would you like a lift home?" "Oh yes, please."; "Yes, please, it's an emergency," [he] answered.

words.definition: a long thin piece of potato that is cooked in oil
examples: fish and chips; I like to eat fish and chips.

words.definition: to stop sleeping or to make someone else stop sleeping
examples: Did you wake up at all during the night?; I woke up with a headache.; Come on, wake up - breakfast is ready.; Can you wake us up at 7, please?; I wake up at 8 o'clock.

words.definition: the number 5
examples: Five, four, three, two, one, blast-off!; I work five days a week.; I will finish work at five o'clock.

words.definition: a bowl that you sit on or stand near when you get rid of waste substances from your body
examples: I was on the toilet when the phone rang.; Don't forget to flush the toilet.; The toilet seat was cracked and there was no paper.; I can remember I left it on the table near the toilet.

words.definition: the number 9
examples: a nine-month prison sentence; The birthday girl was wearing a badge with a nine on it.; I start college at half past nine.

words.definition: the number 15
examples: thirteen, fourteen, fifteen, sixteen; "How many books were returned?" "Fifteen."; She's invited fifteen children to her party.; It is fifteen years old and it is in good condition.

words.definition: a large amount or number of people or things
examples: She eats lots of fruit.; There were a lot of people there.; I've got a lot to do today.; He does lots of travelling in his job.; We met lots of people on holiday.

words.definition: an adult female person
examples: a 30-year-old woman; She's a really nice woman.; A woman and two men were arrested on the day after the explosion.; Women first got the vote in Britain in 1918.; Your teacher will be a woman.

words.definition: the number 17
examples: sixteen, seventeen, eighteen; Is that a seventeen on the front of that bus?; He is seventeen years old.

words.definition: used to tell someone how pleased you are about something they have done
examples: "I passed my exam." "Well done!"

words.definition: the activity or skill of getting information from books, newspapers, etc.
examples: I did a lot of reading on holiday.; Both children find writing difficult but their reading is fine.; The diaries make good bedtime reading.; Also we do some practice task[s] [on] writing, reading, speaking and spelling.

words.definition: the number 14
examples: twelve, thirteen, fourteen, fifteen; Her baby is fourteen months old.; Several days ago I had my birthday and I am now fourteen.

words.definition: the number 20
examples: nineteen, twenty, twenty-one; space for twenty people; I think we were twenty people.

words.definition: the number 10
examples: I've invited ten people.; They met ten years ago.; This is only ten minutes [away] by car.

words.definition: something you say to greet someone in the evening
examples: Good evening, everyone.

words.definition: to wake up and get out of bed, or make someone do this
examples: I had to get up at five o'clock this morning.; Could you get the kids up?; My friend gets up early.

words.definition: the number 2
examples: They've got two houses.; I spent two years in Ethiopia.; It's two o'clock.; He'll be two (years old) in February.; I go to college two days per week.

words.definition: used to say politely that you want something
examples: I'd like a cup of coffee, please.; I'd like to talk to her myself.; I'd like fish and chips (but not too fat[ty]!)

words.definition: to have a particular name
examples: a boy called Adam; Their latest album is called "In Rainbows".; My friend is called Jessica.

words.definition: used for saying goodbye to someone you are going to meet again later/soon/tomorrow, etc.
examples: I'll see you later!; See you soon.

words.definition: one of the hard white objects in the mouth, which are used for biting and chewing
examples: front/back teeth; a broken/missing tooth;  false teeth;  Brush/Clean your teeth thoroughly morning and night.; I had to have a tooth out.

words.definition: a small plastic card that allows you to buy something and pay for it later
examples: I paid by credit card.; The wallet contains all my credit cards and my ticket to London.

words.definition: the programmes that you hear when you listen to the radio
examples: We heard him speaking on the radio this morning.
;  I listen to the radio in the evening.
; He likes watching television and listening [to the] radio.

words.definition: to stop living or existing
examples: Twelve people died in the accident.; She died of/from hunger/cancer/a heart attack/her injuries.; It is a brave person who will die for their beliefs.; Our love will never die.; The pen is very important for me because my grandfather g[a]ve it to me before he died.

words.definition: the number 8
examples: She was eight years old when her family moved here.; We've got eight people coming to dinner.; I will arrive at eight in the morning.

words.definition: something you say to someone when you meet them in the afternoon
examples: Good afternoon, Cara.

words.definition: something you say to greet someone when you meet them in the morning
examples: Good morning, Joe - how are you today?; When you come in clas[s] he say[s] hi good morning every body.

words.definition: during the early part of the day
examples: I listen to the radio in the morning.; She goes to the college in the morning and [at] night she goes to work.

words.definition: a place where especially alcoholic drinks are sold and drunk, or the area in such a place where the person serving the drinks stands
examples: I met him in a bar in Budapest.; There weren't any free tables, so I sat at the bar.; Why don't you ask the guy behind the bar?; Every day she works in the hotel and [a] bar.

words.definition: the unit of money used in the US, Canada, Australia, New Zealand and some other countries
examples: Can I borrow ten dollars?; The suitcase was full of dollar bills.; Eugene gave me twenty dollars.

words.definition: a woman who works in a restaurant, bringing food to customers
examples: She's working as a waitress at the moment.; She is a waitress [and] she likes this job.
